Definition: a primary verb; to hear (in various senses):--give (in the) audience (of), come (to the ears), (shall) hear(-er, -ken), be noised, be reported, understand.
BiblicalUsage: The commonest hearing word in the New Testament — hundreds of times. Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time; He that hath ears to hear, let him hear; The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Hearing is the doorway of the whole gospel: the dead hear His voice and live.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hearing is the Bible's first act of faith. The deaf hear, the dead hear, and the living are told to hear — and the promise is that the voice of the Son of God does not merely inform, it raises. That is why Jesus keeps saying, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
RelatedTopics: Faith; Listening Well; Word of God
